title: UNIT 4: CELL REPRODUCTION
notes:
✓ Cell reproduction is the process by which cells divide to produce new cells.

→ The main types of cell division are mitosis and meiosis.

title: 4.1 CELL CYCLE
notes:
✓ The cell cycle is the sequence of events that occurs in a parent cell as it grows, duplicates its genetic material and divides to form daughter cells.

→ Interphase → preparation and growth stage.
→ Cell division → nuclear division followed by cytoplasmic division (cytokinesis).

✓ The cell cycle ensures that genetic material is copied and distributed to daughter cells.

title: INTERPHASE
notes:
✓ Interphase is the preparation period before cell division. It has three main stages:

◆ G₁ (First Gap) → cell grows, carries out normal activities and produces materials needed for DNA replication.

◆ S (Synthesis) → DNA is replicated so each chromosome produces two sister chromatids.

◆ G₂ (Second Gap) → cell continues growing, produces materials needed for division and prepares for mitosis.

→ G₁ → Growth | S → DNA synthesis | G₂ → Preparation for mitosis

title: CELL-CYCLE CONTROL
notes:
✓ The cell cycle has an internal control system that regulates cell growth and division. Proper control ensures cells divide when needed and prevents abnormal division.

→ Failure of cell-cycle control can cause uncontrolled cell division and may lead to cancer or abnormal tissue growth.

title: 4.2 CELL DIVISION
notes:
✓ Cell division is the process by which a parent cell divides to form daughter cells. It includes:

→ Nuclear division → division of the genetic material.
→ Cytokinesis → division of the cytoplasm.

title: 4.2.1 MITOSIS
notes:
✓ Mitosis is nuclear division in which duplicated chromosomes are equally distributed to form two genetically identical daughter cells with the same chromosome number as the parent cell.
→ It mainly occurs in somatic (body) cells.

→ Main stages: Prophase → Metaphase → Anaphase → Telophase → Cytokinesis.

title: PROPHASE — 'PREPARATION PHASE'
notes:
◆ Duplicated chromosomes condense and become visible.
◆ Each chromosome consists of two sister chromatids joined at the centromere.
◆ The nuclear membrane breaks down.
◆ Centrosomes move toward opposite poles.
◆ Spindle fibres form and attach to chromosomes.

title: METAPHASE — 'ARRANGEMENT PHASE'
notes:
◆ Chromosomes line up along the equator/metaphase plate of the cell.
◆ Spindle fibres attach to the sister chromatids from opposite poles.
✓ Proper alignment ensures equal distribution of chromosomes to the daughter cells.

title: ANAPHASE — 'MIGRATING PHASE'
notes:
◆ Sister chromatids separate at the centromere.
◆ Spindle fibres pull the separated chromatids toward opposite poles.
◆ Each separated chromatid becomes an individual chromosome.
✓ The genetic material is equally distributed between the two future daughter cells.

title: TELOPHASE — 'REVERSE PROPHASE'
notes:
◆ Chromosomes reach opposite poles.
◆ Nuclear membranes reform around each set of chromosomes.
◆ Chromosomes become less condensed.
◆ The mitotic spindle breaks down.
✓ Two new nuclei are formed.

title: CYTOKINESIS
notes:
✓ Cytokinesis is the division of the cytoplasm after nuclear division.

→ Animal cells → the cell membrane constricts inward, forming a cleavage furrow.
→ Plant cells → a cell plate forms between the two nuclei and develops into a new cell wall.

✓ Result → two genetically identical daughter cells.

title: CHROMOSOME TERMS
notes:
◆ Chromosome → condensed structure containing genetic material.

◆ Sister chromatids → two identical copies of a replicated chromosome joined at the centromere.

◆ Homologous chromosomes → chromosome pairs containing corresponding genetic information, with one chromosome inherited from each parent.

◆ Centromere → region joining sister chromatids and involved in chromosome movement.

◆ Spindle fibres → structures that attach to chromosomes and move them during cell division.

title: 4.2.2 MEIOSIS
notes:
✓ Meiosis is a specialized type of cell division that produces sex cells (gametes). It involves two successive divisions: Meiosis I and Meiosis II.

→ One diploid parent cell → four haploid daughter cells.
→ Chromosome number is reduced by half.
→ Daughter cells are genetically different.
→ Crossing over and independent assortment contribute to genetic variation.

title: MEIOSIS I — REDUCTION DIVISION
notes:
✓ Meiosis I separates homologous chromosomes and reduces the chromosome number from diploid (2n) to haploid (n).

Stages:
1 Prophase I
2 Metaphase I
3 Anaphase I
4 Telophase I + Cytokinesis

title: PROPHASE I
notes:
◆ Chromosomes condense and become visible.
◆ Nuclear membrane breaks down and spindle fibres form.
◆ Homologous chromosomes pair up.
◆ Crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids at chiasmata.
◆ Genetic material is exchanged between homologous chromosomes.

✓ Crossing over increases genetic variation.

title: METAPHASE I
notes:
◆ Homologous chromosome pairs line up at the equator of the cell.
◆ Their orientation is random, producing independent assortment.
◆ Spindle fibres attach to the chromosomes.

title: ANAPHASE I
notes:
◆ Homologous chromosomes separate and move toward opposite poles.
◆ Sister chromatids remain joined.
◆ Each pole receives one chromosome from each homologous pair.

✓ This separation reduces the chromosome number by half.

title: TELOPHASE I & CYTOKINESIS
notes:
◆ Chromosomes reach opposite poles.
◆ Nuclear membranes may reform.
◆ Spindle fibres disappear.
◆ Cytokinesis produces two haploid daughter cells.
◆ The chromosomes still consist of two sister chromatids.

✓ DNA is not replicated again before Meiosis II.

title: MEIOSIS II
notes:
✓ Meiosis II separates sister chromatids. It resembles mitosis but begins with two haploid cells and does not involve another round of DNA replication.

Stages:
1 Prophase II
2 Metaphase II
3 Anaphase II
4 Telophase II + Cytokinesis

title: PROPHASE II
notes:
◆ Chromosomes condense again.
◆ Nuclear membranes break down if present.
◆ Spindle fibres form.
◆ The chromosomes prepare for separation.

title: METAPHASE II
notes:
◆ Chromosomes line up individually along the equator.
◆ Spindle fibres attach to the sister chromatids from opposite poles.

title: ANAPHASE II
notes:
◆ Centromeres divide.
◆ Sister chromatids separate and move toward opposite poles.
◆ Each chromatid becomes an individual chromosome.

title: TELOPHASE II & CYTOKINESIS
notes:
◆ Chromosomes reach opposite poles.
◆ Nuclear membranes reform.
◆ Chromosomes become less condensed.
◆ Cytokinesis divides the cytoplasm.

✓ Final result → four genetically different haploid daughter cells.

title: MITOSIS vs MEIOSIS
notes:
✓ MITOSIS
◆ One division
◆ Mainly somatic cells
◆ Produces 2 daughter cells
◆ Daughter cells genetically identical
◆ Chromosome number maintained
◆ Used mainly for growth, repair and replacement

✓ MEIOSIS
◆ Two divisions
◆ Produces gametes
◆ Produces 4 daughter cells
◆ Daughter cells genetically different
◆ Chromosome number reduced by half
◆ Crossing over creates genetic variation

notes:

→ He became known for preserving and improving Ethiopia's genetic resources, especially crop diversity.
